name: Kasavu and Kerala Handloom
tagline: Cream and gold-bordered handloom cotton, the fabric of Onam and weddings
summary: Kasavu and Kerala handloom: the cream-and-gold cotton of Onam, Balaramapuram, Chendamangalam and Kuthampully, and how to buy authentic pieces.
description: Kasavu is the gold-coloured (zari) border woven into cream or off-white cotton to make the Kerala sari, mundu (men's lower garment) and set-mundu. It is worn at Onam, Vishu, weddings and temple festivals.
Handloom weaving clusters include Balaramapuram (Thiruvananthapuram), Chendamangalam (Ernakulam) and Kuthampully (Thrissur–Palakkad border), each with a distinctive style.

history.significance: A symbol of Kerala's festive identity and a major handloom livelihood, with several clusters protected by Geographical Indication status.

timeline.event: Weaver families are settled at Balaramapuram under the patronage of Travancore rulers.
Weaving clusters grow around Chendamangalam and Kuthampully; cooperatives are formed in the 20th century.
Kerala handloom receives the Handloom Mark and Geographical Indication protection for several clusters.

keyFacts: Kasavu was historically woven with real gold or silver thread; most today use gold-coloured zari.
Balaramapuram and Chendamangalam handlooms hold Geographical Indication status.
The Handloom Mark certifies handwoven fabric.
Onam is the peak buying season; shop before August to avoid queues.

folklore.title: The Weavers of the Palace
story: The weaving families of Balaramapuram are said to have been brought from Tamil Nadu to weave fine cloth for the Travancore royal household, and their descendants continue the tradition.
Onam gifts of new clothes (onakkodi) are given by elders to the family, which is why cooperatives report a surge of orders in the weeks before the festival.
folklore.note: Origin accounts are oral and may vary; confirm with weaver cooperatives.

spiritual.summary: Wearing kasavu to a festival or temple is an act of belonging and festivity.

experiences.title: Visit a weaving village
experiences.text: Watch weavers at Balaramapuram or Chendamangalam work a pit loom and ask about the thread count.

experiences.title: Dress for Onam
experiences.text: Try on a set-mundu with the help of shopkeepers; it is a warm and friendly custom.

spiritual.bestFor: Textile lovers, gift buyers and festival visitors.
mindfulTips: Ask permission before photographing weavers at work.
Pay a fair price; do not bargain on cooperative fixed prices.

visitorInfo.bestTime: July to September for Onam shopping; weaving villages can be visited year-round.
visitorInfo.howToReach: Balaramapuram is about 15 km from Thiruvananthapuram; Chendamangalam is near Kochi; Kuthampully is in Thrissur district.
etiquette: Handloom is slow work; order early for custom pieces.

heritage.materials: Cotton with zari (gold-coloured or real silver-gold) border

whereToSee.name: Chendamangalam handloom cluster
whereToSee.note: Known for cotton weaves and the Chendamangalam Handloom Co-operative.

whereToSee.name: Kuthampully weaving village
whereToSee.note: Weaver colony known for fine kasavu.

whereToBuy.name: Hantex — Kerala State Handloom Development Co-operative
whereToBuy.note: State handloom outlets for kasavu sarees, mundus and set-mundu; look for the Handloom Mark.

whereToBuy.name: Kairali — Kerala State Handicrafts Apex Co-operative Society emporiums
whereToBuy.note: Government-linked craft emporiums in major towns; fixed prices and craft-certified items.

whereToBuy.name: Balaramapuram and Kuthampully weaver cooperatives
whereToBuy.note: Buy direct from society showrooms (verify current shops).

experiences.name: Sargaalaya — Kerala Arts and Crafts Village, Iringal
experiences.note: Craft village near Vadakara where artisans work and sell; allow half a day.

experiences.name: Kerala Handloom heritage visits
experiences.note: Ask Hantex or Kerala Tourism for guided weaving-village visits.

buyingTips: Look for the Handloom Mark and ask for the weaver's society name.
Real zari is heavier and does not rub off; ask for a sample.
Wash first in cold water and dry in shade.
